fieldMarks: Much larger than crows: 56-69 cm, wingspan about 116-118 cm
Wedge-shaped tail, very thick bill and shaggy throat feathers
Deep, varied, guttural croaking; a hollow wonk-wonk
In the Southwest, compare to Chihuahuan Raven
behavior: Mostly a permanent resident; some wander in fall and winter south of the breeding range
Typically forages in pairs, sometimes cooperating to flush prey; mostly forages on the ground
Omnivorous opportunist: carrion, garbage, insects, rodents, lizards, frogs and eggs and young of other birds
habitat: Boreal and mountain forests, coastal cliffs, tundra and desert; may also live on prairies if suitable nest sites such as cliffs are nearby.
range: Resident from northernmost North America south to southern Baja California, Nicaragua and Texas, and east of the Rockies to southern Saskatchewan, northeastern Minnesota, northern Michigan and southern New England; also Greenland, Iceland and the Old World.
